'''Naoto T. Ueno''' (born March 1964, Kyoto, Japan<ref>{{Cite web |last=Piana |first=Ronald |date=January 25, 2024 |title=New Director of the University of Hawaii Cancer Center, Naoto T. Ueno, MD, PhD, FACP, Is Also a Two-Time Cancer Survivor |url=https://ascopost.com/issues/january-25-2024/new-director-of-the-university-of-hawaii-cancer-center-naoto-t-ueno-md-phd-facp-is-also-a-two-time-cancer-survivor/ |access-date=2024-10-14 |website=The ASCO Post |language=en}}</ref>) is Director of the University of Hawaiʻi (Mānoa) Cancer Center,<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-10-14 |title=Naoto T. Ueno announced as new UH Cancer Center director {{!}} University of Hawaiʻi System News |url=https://www.hawaii.edu/news/2022/10/14/ueno-uh-cancer-center-director/ |access-date=2024-10-14 |language=en-US}}</ref> one of the 74 NCI National Cancer Centers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-07 |title=Find an NCI-Designated Cancer Center - NCI |url=https://www.cancer.gov/research/infrastructure/cancer-centers/find |access-date=2024-10-14 |website=www.cancer.gov |language=en}}</ref>  He was formerly Professor of Medicine at [[The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center]], and was also a visiting professor with the [[Keio University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://faculty.mdanderson.org/Naoto_Ueno/|title=Naoto Tada Ueno, M.D., Ph.D., F.A.C.P. - Breast Medical Oncology - Faculty - MD Anderson Cancer Center|publisher=[[University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center]]|access-date=25 December 2011|archive-date=January 5, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105034128/http://faculty.mdanderson.org/Naoto_Ueno/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  Ueno's research is in the area of [[inflammatory breast cancer]] and the molecular mechanism of metastasis and tumorigenicity.

He is a breast medical oncologist who specializes in inflammatory, triple-negative, and metastatic breast cancer. He is best known for his preclinical development of [[Adenovirus early region 1A|E1A]] gene therapy and multiple preclinical developments, which led to novel clinical trials related to inflammatory and triple-negative breast cancer.

Ueno moved from Texas to the [[University of Hawaiʻi]] to be director in December 2022.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 9, 2023 |title=New UH Cancer Center director shares vision for future &#124; University of Hawaiʻi System News |url=https://www.hawaii.edu/news/2023/01/09/ueno-shares-uh-cancer-center-vision/}}</ref> He also practices at Queen's Medical Center and Kapiolani Children and Women's Hospital. 

Dr. Ueno studies cancer metastasis, MAPK/EGFR pathways, and cancer microenvironment. He previously was the executive director of the Morgan Welch Inflammatory Breast Cancer Program and Clinic and Section Chief of the Translational Breast Cancer Research at the Department of Breast Medical Oncology at the Anderson Cancr Center. 

He is the founder of the Japan TeamOnclogy Program and CancerX.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mdanderson.org/publications/conquest/cancer-care-in-japan.h36-1585890.html|title=MD Anderson takes its 'normal' to Japan|first=Sandi|last=Stromberg|website=MD Anderson Cancer Center}}</ref>

== Awards ==
*1995-1996	 Clinical Fellow Research Award, MD Anderson Cancer Center
*1996	 Cancer Research Achievement Award, MD Anderson Cancer Center
*1996	 Houston Endowment, Jesse H. Jones Fellowship in Cancer Education
*1996	 Outstanding Achievement in Cancer Research Award, Pharmacia and Upjohn
*1998	 American Association Cancer Research-Glaxo Wellcome Oncology Clinical Research Scholar Award for Promising Translation or Clinical Research, Glaxo Wellcome
*2008	 6th Robert M. Chamberlain Distinguished Mentor Award Nomination (Top Three Finalist), MD Anderson
*2011	 Amgen Basic Research Award, 2nd Prize for Mentoring, MDACC
*2013	 Regent's Outstanding Teaching Award, University of Texas
*2013	 Bradley Stuart Beller Special Merit ASCO Merit Award for Hiroko Masusda, MD, PhD (Mentee)
*2018	 Rune for the Cure Foundation. Unknown Hero Award.
